classes.name: EAGLAnim::FnAnim
classes.comment: Root of the EAGLAnim channel/blender hierarchy (PS2 sheet EAGLAnim::FnAnim: Eval, EvalSQT, EvalEvent, GetType, GetAttribute...). Xbox: vptr +0, fields +4/+8. PS2 (GCC): fields +0/+4, vptr +8, so derived fields from +0xc sit at the same offset on both builds. Vtable 0x1a0c6c (15 slots) is restored last by FnRunBlender/FnTurnBlender destructors.

fields.name: unk4
fields.evidence: zeroed by every ctor (FnAnimMemoryMap ctor faa80, FnRunBlender 105000, FnTurnBlender 1042d0); PS2 +0 zeroed (FnRunBlender ctor 279328). Name invented

fields.name: type
fields.evidence: ctors store a per-class id as a dword (CompoundChannel 0xf, RunBlender 8, TurnBlender 9, DeltaQ 0x11, DeltaF3 0x14); PS2 +4 same values (279328: 8, 268bc8: 0x11). Callers deleting sub-anims read it as a word to index the per-type free list 0x2414b0 (dtors 105050, fab60). GetType on sheet. +0xa presumably padding/high half

notes: Shared bases from the PS2 sheet: EAGLAnim::FnAnim (vtable 0x1a0c6c, 0xc bytes) and EAGLAnim::FnAnimMemoryMap (ctor faa80, dtor faaa0, vtable 0x1a1130, 0x10 bytes). FnRunBlender/FnTurnBlender derive FnAnim directly with its ctor inlined; FnCompoundChannel and FnDeltaF1/F3/Q derive FnAnimMemoryMap. GCC puts FnAnim's vptr at +8 after its two fields, so all derived offsets agree on both builds.
FnAnim +8 is written as a dword but read as a word to index the free list at 0x2414b0 when sub-anims are deleted (vtable slot 0 call, then push onto list), so the type id doubles as a pool index.

0x106780(n) returns &table[n] (12-byte entries at 0x241ba0); FnRunBlender dtor releases entry 0 and FnTurnBlender entry 1 via 0x106750 when their count field is non-zero: a shared per-blender-type buffer.

FnTurnBlender +0x10/+0x14 are passed as this to FnRunBlender::ComputeBeginRootQ/ComputeEndRootQ on both builds; either the turn blender holds two run blenders, or those functions are generic root-Q helpers misfiled under FnRunBlender. Typed as FnRunBlender * (medium).

Suspected misname: Xbox 0x105e00 'FnRunBlender::GetFrequency' is 0xf0 bytes and writes +0x48 (frequency), while PS2 GetFrequency 279808 is an 8-byte accessor. Likely SetSpeed(float) (sheet row, no Xbox match yet). Not verified; no return type given.
FnDeltaF1 InitBuffersAsRequired (feae0) sizes not checked; F1 fields assumed to mirror F3 (same offsets, same ctor pattern, same dtor gate).
FnCompoundChannel is 0x18 on Xbox and 0x1c on PS2 (bool packing at +0x14/+0x15).
